messages.subject: Re: Using Maaslin on R: how to install Maaslin?
parts:
Dear Himel and Maaslin community,

I have an additional question regarding the forcing of predictors in Maaslin.

In the Maaslin help documentation on R, it is stated that: 
strForcedPredictors : Metadata features that will be forced into the model seperated by commas. These features must be listed in the read.config file. Example '-F Metadata2,Metadata6,Metadata10'.

With the PCL file attached and knowing that I want to force AGE, SEX, BV0, and Tob into my model, I have tried to modify my CONFIG file to make it look like this:

Matrix: Metadata
Read_PCL_Rows: -Tob

Matrix: Abundance
Read_PCL_Rows: Bacteroidetes-

-F AGE,SEX,BV0,Tob

And my R-code to look like that:

Maaslin('CoarsePhylum.pcl','maaslin_output',strInputConfig='CoarsePhylum_maaslin.read.config', dSignificanceLevel=0.10, strForcedPredictors=AGE,SEX,BVO,Tob)

But I get an error message saying that my AGE object is not found...

My take on that would be that either my R code or my CONFIG file (or both...) have one or multiple errors... Could you please enlighten me as per the correct syntax to force predictors?
I would be very grateful!

Thanks a lot for your help and support!

Valentin

messages.author: 3bf2dfbdb300e013
messages.subject: Re: Using Maaslin on R: how to install Maaslin?
parts:
Hi Valentin,

Since you are calling the function within R, you need to specify the forced predictors using standard vector notation in R. For your specific example, this will translate to strForcedPredictors=c(‘AGE’, ‘SEX’, ‘BVO’, ‘Tob’) in your MaAsLin function. The comma-separated values will be required when you will call MaAsLin from the command line. Hope this helps.

Many thanks,
Himel
